summary: The note surveys how regions of the world are building cybersecurity workforce pipelines as of late 2023 to 2024. It covers the US collaborative approach (CETAP, apprenticeships, CyberCorps), the EU's policy-driven strategy, varied Asia-Pacific programs, efforts in the developing world, and the role of industry partners. It concludes that scale, speed, and training quality remain challenges, requiring adaptive national strategies.
one_line: A global overview of national and regional strategies, programs, and industry partnerships for building a skilled cybersecurity workforce, and the challenges that remain.
key_facts: Dianne Russell, CISA Director, in an address dated October 10, 2023, stressed a collaborative approach among academia, industry, and government to create a cybersecurity talent pipeline.
The Cybersecurity Education and Training Assistance Program (CETAP) received additional funding in an initiative announced November 15, 2023, and provides K-12 educators with curricular resources.
The National Science Foundation sponsors the CyberCorps: Scholarship for Service program, which aims to strengthen the federal cyber workforce exclusively.
The European Cybersecurity Strategy was revised in June 2024, with Commissioner Mariya Gabriel among those spearheading efforts to harmonize cybersecurity education across EU member states.
The European Cybersecurity Competence Centre was established in early 2024 in Bucharest, Romania, to coordinate research and disseminate best practices in cybersecurity training.
The Digital Europe Programme addresses the cybersecurity skills shortage through upskilling professionals and cross-border training exercises.
Singapore's Cyber Security Agency (CSA) announced the 'Cybersecurity Career Mentoring Program' on September 5, 2023, for hands-on learning experiences for students.

South Korea's Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA) announced the 'Cyber Star Korea' program in December 2023 to identify and develop top young talent via national competitions and incubation programs.
The African Union's Malabo Convention (Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection) set the stage for greater cooperation on workforce development among African states.
The African Cybersecurity Resource Center was launched on February 21, 2024, providing training resources for professionals across Africa.

The Organization of American States, through its Inter-American Committee against Terrorism (CICTE), offers cross-regional training and helped Colombia and Peru develop national cybersecurity strategies.
Google, IBM, and Microsoft have established their own cybersecurity training programs to fill the gap between academic knowledge and practical skills.
IBM's New Collar initiative redefines pathways to tech jobs by emphasizing skills and aptitudes over traditional degrees.
Persistent challenges include the scale, speed, and quality of training needed to keep pace with emerging threats.
